lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Make the phone format consistent with the country where you are applying.
items.because: The country code is useful for international applications.

items.says: Make sure the portfolio URL is clickable in the PDF and leads directly to a polished portfolio.
Provide access instructions if the portfolio requires a password.
Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It does not establish your qualifications and creates privacy and bias risks.

items.says: Remove the nationality unless it is specifically required.
items.because: Work authorization is more relevant, and nationality itself usually is not.

items.says: Consider omitting the location if space becomes tight.
items.because: The degree and institution are more important.

items.says: Add a relevant concentration, thesis, honors, or coursework only if it strengthens your UX research positioning.
Clarify whether 37% and 22% compare test and control groups or pre- and post-test performance.
items.because: An A/B test implies a comparison between variants.

items.says: Provide sample size or statistical confidence in the portfolio if available.
items.because: A four-week test may not establish a reliable result without sufficient volume.

items.says: Ensure that “saved progress” describes what the product actually did.
A 3:1 contrast ratio does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for normal body text.
items.because: Normal-sized text generally requires 4.5:1; 3:1 applies to large text and certain other cases.

items.says: Verify or narrow the claim about “every background.”
items.because: It includes relevant combinations and states such as hover, focus, disabled, error, and visited links.

items.says: Make your role in the compliance effort precise.
items.because: “Brought the design system to” may imply you personally owned the entire effort.

items.says: Document the testing method or audit scope in the portfolio.
items.because: The specific accessibility claim may be scrutinized.

items.says: Fix the grammatical structure and tense of the bullet beginning “Synthesizing.”
items.because: It begins with a present participle while describing completed work.

items.says: Clarify what changes based on the research cut repeat support calls.
items.because: The research synthesis itself did not necessarily cut calls.

items.says: State the comparison period for the 23% reduction if available.
Include only methods that were materially used.
items.because: The density of methods otherwise makes the result harder to understand.

items.says: Specify the issue category behind “about statements” if possible.
items.because: The phrase is somewhat broad.

items.says: Clarify whether you made or prioritized the recommendations rather than only presenting findings.
Explain what made the fixes the “top five.”
items.because: They could have been highest-impact fixes, stakeholder selections, or your own recommendations.

items.says: Give measurable outcomes for the shipped fixes if possible.
items.because: Shipping shows influence but is weaker evidence than adoption plus impact.

items.says: Give the before-and-after quarterly test counts.
items.because: “Doubled” is less informative without a baseline.

items.says: Clarify how the increased number of tests maintained acceptable quality.
items.because: Increased quantity alone can raise questions about rigor.

items.says: Reflect the full scope of your enablement or governance contribution, not just the script template.
items.because: The repeatable process may have been the more important contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether the sign-up figures represent comparable cohorts and whether other changes occurred.
items.because: Other onboarding, marketing, or traffic changes could affect the result.

items.says: Specify what “led research” involved.
items.because: The phrase does not show responsibilities such as study design, recruitment, synthesis, or stakeholder decisions.

items.says: Provide a comparison group or clear pre-launch baseline if available.
items.because: It would make the post-launch claim more credible.

items.says: The stated average recommendation rating is not Net Promoter Score.
items.because: NPS is promoters minus detractors as percentages, not an average 0–10 rating.

items.says: State the comparison period if the figure is an average rating.
Explain your contribution to the metric’s improvement.
items.because: A UX researcher usually influences changes rather than single-handedly raising a product metric.

items.says: Make the connection between the research and the two-way reminder precise.
items.because: “Led to” should be supportable by stakeholders.

items.says: Include the comparison period, cohort, or timeframe if available.
Describe any implementation, experimentation, or operations partnership elsewhere if it was part of the work.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The role has ended.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, maintained, or repeatedly wrote the templates.
items.because: The current tense and phrasing make the timeline unclear.

items.says: Verify the scope of “all patient studies.”
items.because: It is a broad claim.

items.says: Explain what the measured “setup time” included if space permits.
items.because: It could mean recruitment, approvals, or study preparation.

items.says: Specify the study’s criteria for “older patients” in the portfolio.
items.because: The term is imprecise, particularly if age was an accessibility factor.

items.says: Clarify the support-call measurement window and whether volume was adjusted for telehealth visits.
Avoid implying that testing alone cut support calls.
items.because: The redesigned interface and its implementation were also part of the causal chain.

items.says: Consider emphasizing the project’s research scope, accessibility methods, or deliverable instead of Figma.
items.because: Figma is a tool, not necessarily the most important project descriptor.

items.says: Distinguish completed findings from planned work in this ongoing project.
Avoid implying deployed, real-world impact if this is an independent concept.
items.because: The impact may extend only to the study.

items.says: Clarify whether participants included both screen-reader and low-vision users, and whether the map was screen-reader accessible.
items.because: Being evaluated with screen readers is not necessarily the same as being accessible to them.

items.says: Specify the testing format in the portfolio.
items.because: It is unclear whether testing was moderated, remote, or in person.

items.says: Avoid presenting the 12-person study as broadly representative.
items.because: Twelve participants can be appropriate for qualitative usability work.

items.says: The reduction from 90 to 60 seconds is about 33%, not a 50% improvement.
items.because: It is a 30-second reduction from a 90-second baseline.

items.says: Say whether “improvement” means faster completion or reduced time.
items.because: Improvement is ambiguous for a time-based measure.

items.says: Qualify the attribution to audio landmarks and high-contrast colors if their effects were not isolated.
items.because: The study may not have compared them separately or against a control condition.

items.says: Present the result as a study finding, not validated population-level impact.
items.because: The sample is small.

items.says: Calling the change from 65% to 85% a 20% increase confuses percentage points with relative change.
items.because: It is 20 percentage points, or approximately a 31% relative increase.

items.says: Reduce the repetition of the preceding bullet’s intervention and participant count.
items.because: It makes the project feel less substantial and may look like metrics were split to inflate impact.

items.says: Make clear that this and the preceding bullet report distinct measures, and explain the testing comparison.
Define “task success.”
items.because: It could mean completion without assistance, within a time limit, or under another criterion.

items.says: Clarify your individual responsibilities within the three-person team.
items.because: Recruiters need to know what you personally did.

items.says: Consider emphasizing research, design, or implementation scope rather than Figma.
items.because: Figma is less informative if space is limited.

items.says: Clarify why phone bookings fell.
items.because: Online bookings, demand, or another process may have changed.

items.says: Check that the underlying booking count supports the “by a quarter” claim.
Clarify whether the booking flow was deployed.
items.because: Readers may otherwise assume it was only a prototype.

items.says: Explain the recruitment and consent process behind “hallway testing” in the portfolio.
items.because: The term can sound informal, particularly in a health-related setting.

items.says: Explain how you determined that the six issues prevented completion.
Avoid implying statistical validation from the ten participants.
items.because: Ten participants are reasonable for finding usability problems.

items.says: Clarify your direct contribution to the Spanish-language booking addition.
items.because: The wording may imply the handbook alone caused that work.

items.says: Specify the handbook’s maintenance scope in the portfolio if relevant.
items.because: It could include content governance, accessibility checks, translation workflow, or technical updates.

items.says: Separate software tools from screen-reader testing and other capabilities.
items.because: The current “Tools” category mixes tools with a method.

items.says: Include relevant analytics, survey, recruiting, repository, or prototyping platforms used in the roles if applicable.
items.because: They may be relevant to target jobs.

items.says: Correct the spelling of “interveiws.”
Make capitalization and punctuation consistent.
List A/B testing as a method only if you personally designed, analyzed, or interpreted tests.
Add other relevant methods only if the experience supports them.
items.because: The methods list could be stronger, but additions should be genuine.

items.says: Use consistent date spacing and dash style throughout.
Give experience metrics more methodological context.
items.because: Sample size, comparison period, baseline, and your specific contribution are not always clear.

items.says: Prioritize bullets relevant to the job description rather than letting the résumé become crowded.
items.because: Adding detail to the six-bullet senior role could crowd the page.

items.says: Keep the projects from competing with stronger professional experience.
items.because: The professional roles provide stronger evidence.
